A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on high-dimensional clipped SGD, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGD simulations in Figures 1 and 4 and intrinsic-dimension measurements for ResNet18 and ViT on CIFAR10 in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and neural-network measurements and adds real-data risk trajectories, heuristic-schedule experiments, and clipping-factor diagnostics.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a one-parameter scheduling procedure: c(t) = κ sqrt(2R_t + σ²), with learning rate η(t) max(1, 1/κ). This is a substantive alternative to the retained max-CCC numerical optimization and exact learning-rate compensation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Cauchy-noise simulations, a binary CIFAR10 random-feature regression task, and Wikitext2 next-token data represented using GPT-2 embeddings. CIFAR10 already appeared in v1's neural-network diagnostics, but the new linear-model prediction experiment has distinct task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 4 expands the max-CCC clipped-SGD versus unclipped-SGD comparison with the approximate optimal heuristic and its ODE counterpart. The original methods remain, making this a limited expansion of the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: New protocols include binary CIFAR10 labels, tanh random features, Wikitext2 contexts of at most 512 tokens, and fitted Gaussian or Gaussian-mixture residual models. Appendix C.2 adds diagnostics at clipping thresholds 0.1, 1, and 10 during unclipped neural-network training. The additional Gaussian condition with intrinsic dimension 281.63 from v1 Figure 1 is omitted.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds Student-t degrees-of-freedom sensitivity analysis and measurements of μ, ν, CSC, and CCC across clipping thresholds in ResNet18 and ViT. Figure 9 adds residual-distribution diagnostics. These substantially extend v1's noise-family comparisons and retained intrinsic-dimension analysis.

E5.justification: The new CIFAR10 and Wikitext2 experiments specify 80% confidence intervals over 50 runs. Synthetic comparisons retain 80% intervals over 100 runs. This adds a distinct repeated-run count without establishing any increase in repetitions for existing experiments.

E6.justification: New results show ODE agreement with Cauchy-noise and real-data trajectories, heuristic schedules closely tracking max-CCC, and additional Student-t and neural-network factor trends. Figure 4's existing Gaussian risk trajectories also change; omitted covariance details prevent interpreting this as a matched-setting performance gain. The original intrinsic-dimension findings are retained.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces Theorem 8, Corollary 1, regularity assumptions, and derivations of reduction-factor scaling bounds. v2 also adds an infinite-variance SDE reformulation and nonlinear factor definitions. The original central theorems largely persist, but the new corollary inconsistently states a bound on ν² while its proof treats ν.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add claims that the deterministic dynamics predict CIFAR10 and Wikitext2 trajectories and that a single-parameter heuristic achieves near-optimal scheduling. These expand the stated contributions beyond v1's dynamical theory and clipping criteria; the principal Gaussian-noise and stability claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a central-limit explanation for Gaussian approximations on non-Gaussian inputs and conditional interpretations of clipping benefits for ResNet18 versus ViT. Appendix C.2 identifies nonlinear approximation fidelity and unproven schedule dominance as limitations. The conclusion removes v1's suggestion that discarding large gradients preserves descent while further reducing variance.

D1.justification: Appendices C.2 and H add factor-estimation implementation guidance, software choices, embedding and residual-fitting procedures, and experiment hyperparameters. Code access instructions change from supplementary materials to a GitHub link, and reported simulation hardware changes from Colab CPU to an M1 MacBook Air. Conversely, earlier synthetic covariance specifications and Figure 4 dimension details disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to GPT-2 by Radford et al. and scikit-learn by Pedregosa et al. for the new experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior clipping and high-dimensional SGD theory remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'A Clipped Trip' to 'To Clip or not to Clip.' Localized rewrites update the abstract and dynamics explanation, while new subsections organize scheduling and supplementary experiments. Most existing exposition and proof structure remain intact; citations switch to author-date style.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from two to four panels, Figure 4 adds heuristic curves and legend entries, and new figures display Student-t sensitivity, neural diagnostics, and noise histograms. v1 Figure 5 is retained as v2 Figure 8. v2 Figures 6 and 7 duplicate the same diagnostic plots with different captions.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful real-data validation, a simple scheduling heuristic, and nonlinear diagnostics. However, its new theoretical support contains substantive inconsistencies: Corollary 1 switches between ν² and ν, and Equation 198 double-counts a tail contribution, allowing its lower bound to exceed Equation 197's upper bound. Existing Figure 4 trajectories also change while covariance details disappear. These unresolved correctness and reporting problems make the net quality effect uncertain despite the substantial additions.
